sources.sweepMetres: Her rider sits at her middle and the blade swept at arm's length works some 0.7 m beyond her gunwale, 0.2 + 0.7 m out: 0.9 m
sources.handsAboveWaterMetres: Astride her bundles 0.12 m above the water, and a seated man's shoulders stand about 0.6 m over his seat (NASA-STD-3000, sitting shoulder height of a 50th-percentile man, 0.59 m)
sources.sideDrag: Round bundles with tapered, upturned ends: the round-bilged hull's cross-flow drag

sources.weight: Her two bundles are 288 reeds, 144 each, and her ties, lashings and ends eight ropes of six reeds: at the rush mat's calibration, a game reed is about 0.15 kg of dry reed (a 1 m² mat of 8 reeds weighs 1 to 1.5 kg as real rushes), 43.2 kg of bundles and 7.2 kg of cord, as a real 1 cm cord weighs 90 g a metre. A caballito de totora 2.44 × 0.41 × 0.23 m weighs 41 kg dry (festival.si.edu, storied objects, reed raft); hers, 3 × 0.36 × 0.18 m of the same build, 43.2 kg
sources.parts: Reed bundles and reed cord, by weight; the cord counts as flax rope
sources.depthMetres: Her bundles stand 18 cm from bottom to top: 144 reeds each, 80 L at the reed's density, drawn round (bin/lib/hulls/reedboat.py)
sources.shell: Bundles of stems, which a blow bends and an edge parts without harm; she comes apart where an edge cuts a lashing. Reed rope, as flax rope, 1 cm thick; by the model, eight ties 0.5 voxel wide along each bundle's 48 voxels and the five lashings across her cover about a tenth of her sides and a twentieth of her bottom. A breaker's pressure bends the stems, which spring back
sources.soak: A caballito of 41 kg dry weighs some 68 kg soaked with sea water after a day's use (festival.si.edu): its reed takes up two thirds of its weight in water a day afloat, 33 kg on her 50.4. Unmeasured, balance on history: the reed saturates at five times its weight, a sunny day ashore drives four times its weight out again, and each drying leaves a third of what it drove out as rot, so a boat soaked and dried a few times is past saving where Titicaca's totora boats, dried after every trip, last months

sources.time: A held action lasts the real time of that one piece of work over sixty: game time runs 30 times faster than real time, and boat work is halved again
sources.lashing: One rope is ten metres of cord, some ten turns pulled tight around both bundles: about a quarter of an hour. Her five lashings of two turns, each with its knot, take 11.8 m, two ropes, counted by her shape's builder; the first binds the bundles into her where they lie
sources.tips: Each end is pulled together and up, and bound in a spiral of turns some six centimetres apart, 8.8 m of cord: one rope an end, a quarter of an hour

sources.ends: Her ends stand up only by the stiffness of their bound reed, against their weight; soaked, the reed is heavier and limp, and they sag as far as she is soaked toward saturation, where they would lie flat. No line holds them up, as none held Ra I's stern

sources.beamMetres: Her two 18 cm bundles side by side
sources.windageSquareMetres: Her 3 m length over a freeboard of about 5 cm with her rider aboard, and her two raised ends
sources.heave: Reed is light and rises with the crest
sources.capsizeBreakerMetres: Huanchaco's caballitos are paddled out through the surf and ride its breakers in (festival.si.edu): the low float slips under a breaker, which rolls her only once it stands as high as her rider sits, about 0.9 m
sources.rollResponse: Bundles bound into a flat-bottomed hull: a little livelier than vanilla's boats
sources.pitchResponse: Light and short, it lifts to each swell
